name: Juvelook
lead: Juvelook is an injectable poly-D,L-lactic acid (PDLLA) product made by VAIM Inc. of Seoul, South Korea, used in aesthetic medicine as a skin booster and collagen-stimulating agent. Published reports describe a PDLLA and hyaluronic acid hybrid formulation, with variants named Juvelook Volume and Juvelook GLAM.[2][7][9]

Published literature consists mainly of case reports, case series and small clinical studies, including use in the tear trough, nasolabial folds, forehead, sunken cheeks, clavicle and facial pores, as well as animal research and case reports of complications such as nodules.[1][2][3][4][8][9][10]
infobox: Tear trough, nasolabial folds, forehead, cheeks, skin texture

paras: Studies have examined Juvelook for lower eyelid or tear trough rejuvenation in Korean women,[2] nasolabial fold correction,[10] lateral sunken cheek (subzygomatic depression),[8] clavicular augmentation using a cannula,[9] forehead augmentation combined with autologous fat transfer,[4] and, in a case series, facial pore reduction with microneedling and topical application.[3]

A 2025 study evaluated the efficacy and safety of Juvelook for tear trough deformities in Korean women.[2] A case series of microneedling combined with topical Juvelook assessed pore size and skin texture.[3] A study on forehead augmentation evaluated 12-month safety, efficacy and volume stability of sequential PDLLA and fat transfer.[4] Further reports address subzygomatic depression, nasolabial folds and clavicular augmentation.[8][10][9]

A case report used ultrasound and radiological patterns to assess collagen stimulation and tear trough enhancement,[5] and a study compared pain between the left and right sides during skin-booster injection.[6] Most of these are small, uncontrolled or case-level evidence.

A case report described a 42-year-old woman who developed firm, non-inflammatory nodules about three weeks after PDLLA injection in the tear trough; the nodules were managed with a monopolar radiofrequency device.[1]
A 2026 rabbit ear study investigated vascular behaviour and tissue response after intra-arterial injection of Juvelook and Juvelook Volume.[7] Animal findings do not establish human risk rates.

card.summary: A Korean PDLLA-hyaluronic acid biostimulator injected for tear troughs, folds and skin texture, supported by small studies and case reports.
card.note: Nodule reports and animal data on intra-arterial injection exist.

quick.overview:
Juvelook is a poly-D,L-lactic acid injectable from VAIM Inc. in Korea, used by clinicians as a skin booster and collagen stimulator in areas such as under the eyes, nasolabial folds, forehead and cheeks.

Published evidence is mostly small studies, case series and case reports, mostly from 2025 and 2026.
quick.mechanism: PDLLA is described as a biostimulator that prompts the body to produce collagen over time. Some Juvelook variants are reported to combine PDLLA with hyaluronic acid.
quick.risks: Reported problems include firm nodules after tear trough injection. A rabbit study examined what happens with accidental intra-arterial injection. Procedures are performed by trained clinicians.
